newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Crude Outlook - Iraq, technicals point lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Crude Outlook - Iraq, technicals point lower.

text.p: U.S. crude oil prices are expected to continue to soften this week as the market prepares for Iraq to resume humanitarian exports under the U.N. oil-for-food plan, analysts and traders said on Monday.

August light sweet crude was trading around $19.30-40 a barrel on the NYMEX early on Monday afternoon, with cash West Texas Intermediate/Cushing running at a two-cent premium to futures based on current exchange-for-physical transactions.
The outright price was trailing a weaker pattern driven by last week's sell-off, which broke key trendlines throughout the oil complex, analysts and traders said.
"I think we're in a little bit of a corrective mode right now," said Tom Bentz, head of the energy division at High Yield Analytics in New York. "We'll probably test $19.20-25, potentially $19.00."
Signs that Iraq shortly would resume limited exports following a period of delays compounded the technical weakness.

On Thursday, Iraq's U.N. coordinator Staffan de Mistura said the aid distribution plan for the oil-for-food deal was complete, and would be submitted to the U.N. for approval following some "fine-tuning."
"Once the news is out about Iraq, I would guess we hold around $19.00 a barrel," said William H. Brown, president of W.H. Brown & Co in New York.
"We may hold there and stay in a relatively narrow range for the rest of the summer," he said.
Cash crude differentials are likely to remain relatively firm, traders said.
"Asphalt-related seasonal tightness" is likely to continue bolstering sour grades, an East Coast trader said.
West Texas Sour/Midland was trading around $1.18-12 discount to WTI on Monday afternoon, up from around minus $1.50 in mid-June.
For their part, sweet grades are expected to continue firm, reflecting the narrow spread between WTI and North Sea Brent.
"Right now, the arbitrage is not favorable. I'd continue to look for strength in LLS (Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James)" said the East Coast trader.
LLS was trading around 19-22 cents premium to WTI, up some 35 cents from mid-June amid scant North Sea sales into the U.S. Gulf Coast.
